target: docs/41-试点课堂Start持久迁移内核SDD.md
focus: profile data and retained test artifacts
sidecar and HMAC-key filesystem permissions and delivery
receipt replay when sidecar is damaged
summary: Application authorization, receipt replay, no-rerun recovery, privacy allowlists, and test-only build isolation are specified well. The SDD does not define enforceable filesystem ACL/mode and key-delivery controls for the case directory, SQLite, sidecar, and HMAC key, and retained crash artifacts have no access/retention policy. HMAC and DB receipt integrity claims depend on these missing controls.

findings.title: Case storage and HMAC key protection are underspecified
findings.evidence: §3 says the supervisor creates the case directory and HMAC key; §5 calls it private and uses an OS-exclusive lifecycle lock; §5/§6 refer to private runtime parameters. No restrictive OS ACL/mode, owner validation, atomic exclusive key creation, or protected key-transfer/no-argv-env rule is specified. The damaged-sidecar receipt-first path verifies DB lifecycle but the stored fingerprint is unkeyed SHA-256.
findings.risk: A local principal able to replace the key and sidecar can forge the HMAC chain; a principal able to write the DB can alter lifecycle rows and recompute an unkeyed fingerprint. The lifecycle lock does not prevent either access.
findings.required_revision: Specify and verify owner-only directory/file permissions on each supported OS; reject unexpected owners/ACL entries; use exclusive restrictive key creation; pass the key through a protected inherited handle/pipe rather than argv/environment; prohibit logging it; define the trusted-local-principal boundary and, if needed, authenticate receipt recovery with a keyed commitment. Add permission/key-exposure negative acceptance cases.

findings.title: Retained failed-case data has no retention/access rule
findings.evidence: §5 preserves failed/crashed artifacts; SQLite/outbox contains synthetic nickname, greeting, and word/meaning content, while the SDD does not specify artifact reader authorization, retention duration, or cleanup triggers.
findings.risk: Local profile/content data and guessable digest inputs may remain available longer or to more users than necessary, especially after crashes or quarantine.
findings.required_revision: Limit artifact access to the supervisor, define cleanup/retention for success, terminal failure, and quarantined cases, and remove DB/WAL/SHM, sidecar, and key together. Keep the slice synthetic-only.

control_dispositions.principal_and_receipt_replay: acceptable_in_test_only_scope; replay requires current active owner and DB lifecycle validation, does not run Planner/Registry; task expiry is required for new commands
control_dispositions.damaged_sidecar_with_receipt: fail_closed_and_quarantine behavior specified; authenticity depends on unresolved local storage protection finding PSK-SEC6-01
control_dispositions.privacy_and_log_minimization: specified; DB fingerprint is not confidentiality and content remains guessable to DB readers
control_dispositions.production_route_build_isolation: specified via pilot_e2e build tags and separate harness; artifact exclusion not runtime-verified
control_dispositions.supervisor_destroy_recreate_authority: not explicit; bind to supervisor-only access and retention policy under PSK-SEC6-02

remaining_conditions: Close PSK-SEC6-01 before approving the SDD security boundary.
Resolve PSK-SEC6-02 before retaining case artifacts outside the active test run.
limitations: No tests or runtime validation were run.
No build artifact, filesystem ACL/mode, key transfer, DB, or recovery path was inspected.
This review does not approve implementation, production deployment, real student data, or classroom readiness.
